metadata.target_chronology: c. 117 AD (Late Trajanic / Early Hadrianic Roman Thrace)
metadata.coordinate_policy: Zero fabricated coordinates. Every coordinate derives from verified archaeological gazetteers (Pleiades, Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire / DARE, Barrington Atlas, ToposText), excavated site records (NAIM-BAS), or documented modern settlement centroids for unexcavated itinerary corridors with explicit uncertainty radii.

project_eight_stops_end.note: Intermediate mansio near the modern Bulgarian-Turkish border; NOT the historical terminus of Via Diagonalis.

project_stops.modern_location: Plovdiv (Central area / Trimontium & Roman Forum), Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Pleiades 216927 / Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire (DARE) / NAIM-BAS
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Metropolis of Thracia (acropolis fortified; lower plain city unfortified until 172 AD; forum, theatre 114-117 AD, road junction, Hebrus bridge)
project_stops.chronology_attested: 4th c. BC – Medieval (active and flourishing in 117 AD)

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Unattested toponym in 117 AD (early roadside taberna at Syrmus crossing; attested as mutatio Sernota in 333 AD)
project_stops.modern_location: Manole / Rogosh area (crossing of Stryama River), Maritsa Municipality, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Manole settlement reference point / Barrington Atlas Map 22 & Madzharov 2009 (10 Roman miles east of Philippopolis)
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Probable roadside relay post / taberna and river crossing over Syrmus (Stryama)
project_stops.chronology_attested: Name attested 333 AD (Itinerarium Burdigalense 568.2); Roman scatter 1st–4th c. AD in corridor

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Praetorium / Taberna (Neronian station of 61 AD; later attested as mutatio Parembole / Paramvole)
project_stops.modern_location: Belozem area (Selishteto / Malkoto Kale locality), Rakovski Municipality, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Belozem epigraphic zone (Neronian inscription of 61 AD) / Madzharov 2009 (alternate eastern corridor index: 42.227, 25.101)
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Imperial roadside praetorium and taberna established under Nero in 61 AD via procurator T. Iulius Ustus
project_stops.chronology_attested: 61 AD epigraphically (Nero building inscription) through 4th–6th c. AD (Itin. Burd. 568.3)
project_stops.omitted_next_station_note: Project sequence omits mansio Cillae (Cherna Gora, 12 mp east of Parembole) before Carassura.

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Carassura (unfortified Thraco-Roman roadside settlement, sanctuary, and road station)
project_stops.modern_location: Kaleto hill between Rupkite and Svoboda, Chirpan Municipality, Stara Zagora Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Excavated archaeological reserve Karasura / Pleiades 216750 / Wendel 2005
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Unfortified roadside settlement, relay post, and pagan sanctuary (Apollo/Asclepius); NO fortification walls or Christian basilicas in 117 AD
project_stops.chronology_attested: Prehistoric – 1st–3rd c. AD Roman settlement – 4th–6th c. AD fortress – 9th–13th c. medieval
project_stops.distance_note: 21 Roman miles total from Parembole (12 mp Parembole -> Cillae + 9 mp Cillae -> Carassura in Itin. Burd. 568.3-4)

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Arzus (mansio and Roman bridge crossing over the Arzus / Sazliyka River)
project_stops.modern_location: Kalugerovo (at the Sazliyka River crossing), Simeonovgrad Municipality, Haskovo Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Pleiades 216714 / Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire (DARE) / Kalugerovo Roman bridge piers
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Major road station (mansio) and masonry/timber-stone bridge crossing over the Arzus (Sazliyka) River
project_stops.chronology_attested: 1st–6th c. AD (active in 117 AD; attested in Itin. Ant., Itin. Burd., Tab. Peut.)
project_stops.distance_note: In Itin. Ant. 137: Cillis -> Opizo XVIII mp -> Arzo XVIII mp (~27 mp from Carassura; Itin. Burd. manuscript figure XI mp from Carassura omits intermediate segment around Pizos)

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Unconfirmed in 117 AD (known solely as mutatio Palae in 333 AD)
project_stops.modern_location: Unconfirmed exact site in the Ovcharovo – Tyanevo – Sakartsi corridor (northwest of Izvorovo / Harmanli), Haskovo Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Midpoint corridor reference between documented modern villages Tyanevo (42.0333, 25.9500) and Ovcharovo (41.9833, 25.9667) matching VII mp from Arzus and XI mp to Castra Rubra (Madzharov 2009; Itin. Burd. 568.6)
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Hypothetical minor relay post; no excavated structure or epigraphic proof for 117 AD

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Castra Rubra / Subzupara (early Roman mansio and road guard-post on the Sakar pass; pre-fortress phase)
project_stops.modern_location: Kaleto / Balabana locality near Izvorovo (south of Kolarovo), Harmanli Municipality, Haskovo Province, Bulgaria
project_stops.coordinate_source: Excavated Kaleto site near Izvorovo (B. Borisov / NAIM-BAS AOR) & Pleiades 501384
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Roman mansio and small pass praesidium alongside preserved ~6 m stone road pavement (the excavated stone fortress at Kaleto dates to late 5th–6th c. AD, NOT 117 AD)
project_stops.chronology_attested: 1st–4th c. AD road station & pavement; late 5th–7th c. AD Early Byzantine fortress; 8th–9th c. medieval
project_stops.omitted_next_station_note: Project sequence omits mutatio Rhamis / Rhamae (Lyubimets area, 7 mp southeast of Castra Rubra) before Burdipta.

project_stops.name_in_117_ad: Burdipta (mansio in the lower Hebrus valley)
project_stops.modern_location: Svilengrad (Hisarya locality) / Momkovo micro-region, Svilengrad Municipality, Haskovo Province, Bulgaria

alternate_site_coordinates.source: Momkovo southern archaeological zone (Madzharov 2009 / NAIM-BAS surveys)

project_stops.coordinate_source: Hisarya fortress hill in Svilengrad & Momkovo survey area / Pleiades 501381
project_stops.site_type_117_ad: Unfortified or lightly enclosed imperial mansio controlling the lower Hebrus corridor toward Uscudama
project_stops.chronology_attested: 1st–4th c. AD Roman mansio; 4th–12th c. Late Antique and medieval fortress/bishopric
project_stops.distance_note: 18 Roman miles from Castra Rubra (7 mp Castra Rubra -> Rhamis + 11 mp Rhamis -> Burdista in Itin. Burd. 568.8-569.2; XX mp from Subzupara in Itin. Ant. 137.6)

supplementary_and_eastern_nodes.status_117_ad: Emporium not yet founded (established 202 AD under Septimius Severus); minor road locality only

supplementary_and_eastern_nodes.name_in_117_ad: Unattested toponym in 117 AD (attested as mutatio Rhamis in 333 AD)

route_segments.label: Philippopolis Eastern Gate and suburban exit
route_segments.evidence: Excavated Roman street/road pavements, Eastern Gate, and linear tumular/flat necropoleis of 1st–2nd c. AD

route_segments.label: Philippopolis – Sernota (Manole) – Parembole (Belozem) alluvial plain
route_segments.evidence: Alluvial shifting of Maritsa and Stryama obliterated continuous pavement; reconstructed via tumular alignments, 10 + 8 mp distances, and the 61 AD Neronian inscription at Belozem

route_segments.label: Parembole (Belozem) – Cillae (Cherna Gora)
route_segments.evidence: Epigraphically anchored endpoints (Belozem 61 AD; Cillae IGBulg III/2 1517); agricultural disturbance along intervening plain

route_segments.label: Cillae (Cherna Gora) – Carassura (Rupkite)
river_crossings: Stara Reka (at the foot of Kaleto, Rupkite)
route_segments.evidence: Excavated roadbed at Carassura and systematic Bulgarian-German archaeological survey (1981–2005)

route_segments.label: Carassura (Rupkite) – Opizo/Pizos (Dimitrievo) – Arzus (Kalugerovo)
route_segments.evidence: Corridor anchored north of the Maritsa by the Pizos Edict (202 AD) at Dimitrievo and Roman bridge piers at Kalugerovo; rejects erroneous southern detour through Dimitrovgrad/Kasnakovo

route_segments.label: Arzus River (Sazliyka) crossing at Kalugerovo
river_crossings: Arzus / Sazliyka (attested Roman masonry bridge piers)
route_segments.evidence: Documented Roman bridge piers and mansio remains at Kalugerovo

route_segments.label: Arzus (Kalugerovo) – Palae (unconfirmed) – Castra Rubra approach
route_segments.evidence: Mutatio Palae remains unconfirmed on the ground; corridor across SW Sakar foothills inferred from VII + XI mp distances

route_segments.label: Castra Rubra (Izvorovo) Sakar pass roadbed
route_segments.evidence: In situ preserved ~6 m stone-paved Roman roadbed with curbstones near Izvorovo / Kolarovo and excavated Kaleto site

route_segments.label: Castra Rubra (Izvorovo) – Rhamae (Lyubimets) – Burdipta (Momkovo/Svilengrad)
route_segments.evidence: Left-bank Maritsa terrace heavily modified by modern E80 / Maritsa motorway; anchored by rescue archaeology and itinerary mileage (7 + 11 mp)

route_segments.label: Burdipta (Svilengrad) – Daphabae – Uscudama/Hadrianopolis (Edirne)
river_crossings: Tonzus / Tundzha and Hebrus / Maritsa approaches at Edirne
route_segments.evidence: Cross-border Maritsa valley corridor reconstructed via Itin. Ant. (XXIV mp) and Itin. Burd. (Daphabae XI mp)

route_segments.label: Uscudama/Hadrianopolis – Burtudizus – Bergule – Drizipara – Tzurulum – Perinthus
river_crossings: Ergene (Agrianes) left-bank tributaries at Babaeski, Lüleburgaz, and Büyükkarıştıran
route_segments.evidence: Major towns/mansiones securely fixed (Edirne, Babaeski, Lüleburgaz, Büyükkarıştıran, Çorlu, Marmara Ereğlisi); inter-station alignments partly overlain by modern D100 and Ottoman Orta Kol

route_segments.label: Perinthus – Selymbria – Rhegium – Byzantium Propontis coastal trunk
route_segments.evidence: Shared eastern trunk of Via Diagonalis and Via Egnatia; preserved Roman road sections west of Silivri, milestones, and lagoon bridge foundations at Küçükçekmece
